reasoning: Both sets come from the same planning toolchain, with matching structure: contract with code-shaped types and fixtures, pipelines with entry sketches, a phased M1 plan, and context packets. B's RL design is better for learning. Each idea gets its own rung: tabular Q, then DQN, then a CNN on the full grid, with ablations that remove the memory, the target copy or exploration. Fish go REINFORCE then PPO, one fish then a school, full view then limited. Predator-prey goes fixed opponents, then naive co-learning, then an opponent pool. A hyperparameter mapping makes the library comparison fair. B also keeps truncation and termination separate in the Transition type. B's golden cases are concrete closed-form oracles with exact boards and numbers, and I checked several by hand: TC-12 0.009, TC-42 1.3775, TC-29/TC-58 distances, TC-07 observation. Its packets give a builder everything needed. A's spec is solid and covers write-ups, but its plan has real holes. TC-17's bound and TC-07's direction are still 'to be re-derived', yet M1-T25 must make TC-17 pass, so that acceptance can't be checked. Its tests and routes files repeat open questions (TC-17 and TC-07 each listed twice, with conflicting text). Its interface task freezes private helper stubs (holm, verdict, guard, check_runs, apply_style). Its thicken tasks are serialized behind spines even though they write separate stub files. Its planned layout omits charts/check.py and charts/style.py. A's milestone split is finer, but M3 ('Check and explain the snake') is close to a leftover milestone, and M1 ships no replay. B's weaknesses are smaller: a stale brief ('Not doing: Designing future environments now') while full specs for S2 and S3 exist; milestones that each cover a whole stage and are large; future-stage fields frozen into RunSettings in M1; and no write-up feature for the 'explain why it works' goal.
